# Foundation Requirements Checklist: P-F000 — Foundation

**Purpose**: Validate the requirements quality of spec.md (and cross-check against plan.md) for
the auth flows, session lifecycle, error/Failure taxonomy, and navigation surfaces delivered by
P-F000, before `/speckit-tasks` proceeds.
**Created**: 2026-10-11
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

## Auth Flow Requirements (Login / Sign-up)

- [ ] CHK001 - Are client-side validation rules (e.g., password minimum length/format) specified for sign-up and login, or is validation fully deferred to the backend? [Gap, Spec §FR-006, §FR-007, Edge Cases]
- [ ] CHK002 - Is the UI distinction (if any) between a retryable failure (timeout/offline) and a non-retryable one (invalid credentials, malformed request) specified — e.g., presence or absence of a retry affordance? [Gap, Spec §FR-004, §FR-015]
- [ ] CHK003 - Is the mechanism for preventing a duplicate account or duplicate session when the app is backgrounded mid-submission specified (e.g., disabling the submit control, idempotent request handling), or left fully to implementation discretion? [Gap, Spec Edge Cases]
- [ ] CHK004 - Is "Criar conta" mode's toggle behavior (FR-008) specified as preserving or clearing already-entered field values when switching between login and sign-up? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-008]

## Session Lifecycle & Expired-Session Overlay

- [ ] CHK005 - Is "usable session" (FR-009) defined precisely enough to distinguish it from "valid," "active," or "renewable," so routing logic is unambiguous? [Clarity, Spec §FR-009]
- [ ] CHK006 - Does the spec specify what "any related background preparation" (FR-010) during the splash state actually consists of, or is this left undefined? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-010]
- [ ] CHK007 - Is it disambiguated whether a second session expiry during overlay dismissal causes the existing overlay to remain displayed throughout, versus being dismissed and then re-shown? [Ambiguity, Spec Edge Cases]
- [ ] CHK008 - Are all elements of "screen state" that must survive the expired-session overlay (FR-013, FR-014, SC-005) enumerated, or is only scroll position given as an example with the rest left to interpretation? [Completeness, Spec §FR-013, §FR-014, SC-005]
- [ ] CHK009 - Is the approximate duration or threshold for the splash state quantified anywhere in the requirements (vs. only as an implementation-level performance target), so "brief" (User Story 3) is testable? [Clarity, Spec User Story 3, §FR-010]
- [ ] CHK010 - Is the relationship between silent background renewal (Assumptions) and the expired-session overlay (FR-013) consistent — i.e., is it clear the overlay only appears after silent renewal has already been attempted and failed? [Consistency, Spec Assumptions, §FR-013]

## Error / Failure Taxonomy (Either<Failure, T>)

- [ ] CHK011 - Does the spec identify where the authoritative, closed set of backend error codes is defined, given FR-004 and the Backend Failure entity assume a fixed taxonomy? [Traceability, Spec §FR-004, Key Entities]
- [ ] CHK012 - Is the mapping from each of the backend's documented error codes to a specific user-facing message (or message category) specified, or only the general requirement that "every error condition" produce "a clear, non-crashing message" (FR-015)? [Gap, Spec §FR-015]
- [ ] CHK013 - For each of the four auth-related calls (sign-up, login, refresh, session-check), are the specific failure modes (timeout, malformed/non-retryable, offline) that requirements expect to be exercised explicitly enumerated, or only described generically via Edge Cases? [Coverage, Spec Edge Cases, §FR-004]
- [ ] CHK014 - Is "retryable flag" (FR-004) requirement's meaning fully specified — i.e., does the spec state what a screen is expected to do differently when a failure is retryable vs. not, beyond showing a message? [Clarity, Spec §FR-004]

## Navigation & Placeholder Screens

- [ ] CHK015 - Is the side menu's required destination set (FR-011: Home/Chat, Meus Registros, Configurações) consistent with the Assumptions section's mention of an optional "Planos de Ação" placeholder entry — i.e., is it clear whether that entry's presence or absence affects FR-011's completeness? [Consistency, Spec §FR-011, Assumptions]
- [ ] CHK016 - Is "clearly-labeled placeholder" (FR-012) specified with any concrete criteria (e.g., required label text, required "not yet available" indication), or left entirely to implementation judgment? [Clarity, Spec §FR-012]
- [ ] CHK017 - Does the spec define what happens if a user attempts an action on a placeholder screen (Meus Registros, Configurações) beyond viewing it — e.g., any inert control feedback — or is "no functional behavior" (FR-012) sufficient to cover all such interactions? [Edge Case, Spec §FR-012, Edge Cases]
- [ ] CHK018 - Is the requirement that the side menu "overlays the current screen without discarding state" (Acceptance Scenario, User Story 4) distinguished clearly from the separate state-preservation requirement for the expired-session overlay (FR-013), so the two mechanisms aren't assumed to share one implementation requirement? [Consistency, Spec User Story 4, §FR-013]

## Requirement Completeness & Consistency (Cross-Cutting)

- [ ] CHK019 - Is the "if at all" qualifier in FR-016 ("any screen or control belonging to one of them MUST exist only as an inert placeholder, if at all") disambiguated — i.e., does the spec make clear under what condition such a control would legitimately not exist at all? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-016]
- [ ] CHK020 - Are the performance thresholds referenced outside spec.md (e.g., <100ms local reflection, >300ms loading-indicator trigger) reflected as a measurable Success Criterion within spec.md itself, or only documented in plan.md's Technical Context? [Consistency, Gap, Spec Success Criteria]
- [ ] CHK021 - Does the spec specify whether the loading indicator required for network calls exceeding a latency threshold applies uniformly to all four auth/session calls, or could some calls be exempt? [Gap, Spec Success Criteria]
- [ ] CHK022 - Is SC-006 ("zero visual values defined outside the single central source") paired with any requirement for how this is verified (e.g., review process, lint rule), or is verifiability left unaddressed? [Measurability, Spec SC-006]

## Dependencies & Assumptions

- [ ] CHK023 - Is the assumption that RF03 (biometric/PIN) "is built immediately after this one" validated as a hard dependency, or could delivery-order changes invalidate the routing behavior specified in Assumptions (splash → login/sign-up directly, overlay → login directly)? [Assumption, Spec Assumptions]
- [ ] CHK024 - Is the assumption that "every error this unit's calls can return is one of the backend's fixed, documented error codes" validated against an actual enumerated list, or merely asserted without a cross-reference? [Assumption, Spec Assumptions]
- [ ] CHK025 - Is the choice of on-device token storage mechanism explicitly scoped as non-normative ("an implementation choice, not fixed by this specification," per Assumptions) consistent with FR-009's requirement that a session "already exists" between launches — i.e., does the spec avoid implying any particular storage guarantee (e.g., survival across app reinstall) that isn't actually required? [Consistency, Spec Assumptions, §FR-009]

## Notes

- Mark items `[x]` only after review confirms the requirement-quality criterion is satisfied
- Leave items unchecked when they still require clarification, correction, or reviewer evaluation
- `/speckit-implement` reads checklist checkbox state as a gate and must not modify markers
- `checklists/requirements.md` has a separate built-in lifecycle maintained by `/speckit-specify` and `/speckit-clarify`
- Add comments or findings inline
- Link to relevant resources or documentation
- Items are numbered sequentially for easy reference
